From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Hi Andrew —

Great questions — answered inline below. I’ve summarized the short answers up front and included attachments with the details.

Short answers: Hosted API should be a good first step for your pilot. Typical p95s for 350-token single-turn generation in us-west-2 are in the 200–450ms range depending on model choice and instance load. Burst handling is supported up to a per-account burst bucket — we can temporarily raise limits for your pilot. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest; we retain request metadata and logs for the configured retention window and can provide audit logs for SOC2 evidence. Auth is API keys by default; we also support scoped tokens and enterprise KMS integrations for Private deployments.

Detailed responses:
- Rate limits & bursting:
  * Limits are applied at the API key (token) level with account-level guardrails. The default evaluation tier is 60 requests/minute and 30k tokens/minute. For pilots we commonly provision a temporary higher burst allowance (for example, 200 rps sustained with a short burst window) — this is what we recommend for your 40 qps steady state with 80 qps occasional spikes. I attached a csv with our hosted-rate-limits.csv showing typical tiers and how to request an increase.

- Latency:
  * p95 is model and config-dependent. For the default medium LLM we demoed, us-west-2 p95s at 350 tokens are typically 250–380ms if you use streaming=false and no batch mixing. If you enable our batching or use the optimized 'low-latency' instance profile we can push lower latency at slightly higher cost.

- Security & logs:
  * Hosted: encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest, SOC2 Type II controls in place, audit logs available for export, and optional longer retention as an add-on. We do not use customer content for training by default (can be controlled in account settings).

- Endpoints & auth (quick reference):
  * Base URL: https://api.redwood.inference/v1
  * Generation endpoint: POST /models/{model_id}/generate
  * Embeddings endpoint: POST /models/{model_id}/embeddings
  * Auth: x-api-key header (we'll issue a scoped key for the pilot).

- Dedicated / Private notes (brief):
  * Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, SLA-backed throughput, capacity isolation — good if you need predictable sustained qps.
  * Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed network & optional on-prem installers — necessary for strict data residency or air-gapped deployments.

I’ve cc'd Rishi (SE) to offer a short technical call. He can walk through tuning (batching, KV cache, model choices) and help configure a temporary rate-limit bump for the pilot. Rishi — are you available tomorrow at 11am PT for a 30-min call?

Attachments: hosted-rate-limits.csv

Thanks — happy to jump on the call tomorrow at 11am PT. A few quick technical notes to set expectations for the session so we can use the time efficiently: 

- For your 40 qps / ~350 token workload: batching will reduce cost but may add a few ms of latency; we can show a config that keeps p95 under 350ms while improving cost by ~10–20% depending on traffic shape.
- KV cache: if you have repeated prefixes (system prompts/boilerplates) enabling prefix caching will cut token compute cost for subsequent requests.
- Warm pools: Hosted supports pre-warmed instances for predictable latency during spikes — we'll propose a small warm pool for your pilot to handle bursts.
- Rate-limit increase: I’ll open an internal request to provision temporary burst capacity for RWI-2093 so we can validate at your target load without hitting throttles during the pilot.

I'll send a calendar invite for 30 minutes and bring a short runbook + a small script that you can run to measure p95 locally using our sample requests.

See you tomorrow —
